name: Balasana (Child's Pose)
noEquipmentAlternative: Chair version: sit with knees apart and rest forearms and forehead on a table with a pillow; or use carpet with a cushion under the forehead

progressions: Hold 60-90 s with breath into the back ribs
Arms forward and walk the fingertips to one side for a side stretch
Knees together with hips fully on the heels, forehead on floor; then Downward Dog or seated forward bend
regressions: Folded blanket or block between seat and heels, forehead on stacked fists or a folded towel
Rolled towel behind the knees and/or under the ankles
Supported on a bolster or pillows, or chair version with forearms and forehead on a table

setupSteps: Mat and space. Lay the mat on a flat, non-slip floor. A carpet or a doubled mat is kinder to the knees and ankles.
Clothes. Fitted track pants or leggings so the hips, knees and ankles show; a loose kurta or dupatta can be tucked in so it does not cover the hips on camera.

Props ready. Folded blanket (or a second pillow) to place between the seat and heels if the hips do not reach; rolled towel for behind the knees or under the ankles; a bolster, a firm pillow or 2–3 stacked pillows for the supported version; a folded towel or blanket under the forehead if it does not reach the floor.
Starting position. Kneel on the mat with the tops of the feet down. Knees apart for the wide version (about mat width, est.), big toes touching; knees together for the knees-together version.
Camera. Phone on a low stool at mat height, 2 m to the side, landscape, so the head, hips, knees and ankles are all in frame (see section 11).

steps.title: Kneel
steps.action: kneel on the mat with the tops of the feet flat and the big toes touching.
steps.feel: weight even on both knees, ankles comfortable.
steps.visualCheck: side view, shins flat, back long; front view, knees level.

steps.title: Open the knees
steps.action: slide the knees apart to about mat width, keeping the big toes touching.
steps.feel: stretch along the inner thighs, no pinch at the knees.

steps.title: Sit the hips back
steps.action: move the hips back toward the heels, keeping the back long, as far as it feels comfortable (see step 3b for a gap).
steps.feel: gentle stretch through the low back and the front of the thighs.
steps.visualCheck: side view, hips moving back, not the back rounding first.

steps.title: Fold forward
steps.action: bend from the hips and lower the torso between or over the thighs.
steps.feel: weight of the belly on the thighs, a gentle stretch in the back.
steps.visualCheck: side view, back long and gently rounded, not collapsed.

steps.title: Rest the forehead
steps.action: let the forehead rest on the mat, a folded towel or stacked fists, so the neck is long and relaxed.
steps.visualCheck: front view, head hanging evenly, no twisting.

steps.title: Place the arms
steps.action: stretch the arms forward with palms down (more shoulder stretch) or lay them back along the thighs with palms up (more relaxed; the Balasana version in some schools).
steps.feel: shoulders heavy, away from the ears.

steps.title: Hold and breathe
steps.action: stay still, breathing slowly and sending the breath into the back ribs.
steps.feel: light effort 3–4/10 on the ACSM 0–10 effort scale (= Borg 9–11 on the 6–20 scale); a feeling of rest, never pain.
steps.breathing: slow breaths in through the nose and out through the nose or mouth, 5 to 10 breaths.
steps.visualCheck: body still, ribs moving slightly with each breath.

steps.title: Come out
steps.action: walk the hands back toward the knees and roll up slowly, one vertebra at a time, head last.
steps.visualCheck: no sudden jump up; pause a breath kneeling before standing.

commonMistakes.title: Forcing the hips to the heels with sore knees
commonMistakes.text: Forcing the hips to the heels with sore knees. Deep knee bending can pinch or aggravate the knee. Fix: put a folded blanket between the seat and heels, roll a towel behind the knees, or skip the pose; stop if knee pain persists (Expanding Light, DoYouYoga, Bodybyyoga).

commonMistakes.title: Letting the ankles crunch
commonMistakes.text: Letting the ankles crunch. Tops of the feet on a hard floor can be painful. Fix: a rolled towel under the ankles (Ekhart, Yogahealthy blog) or a thicker mat.

commonMistakes.title: Hanging the head with no support
commonMistakes.text: Hanging the head with no support. Neck and shoulder strain. Fix: forehead on a stack of fists, a block or a folded towel, or a bolster.

commonMistakes.title: Collapsing into the back (a sharply rounded spine)
commonMistakes.text: Collapsing into the back (a sharply rounded spine). The stretch goes to the ribs and the neck takes the weight. Fix: hips back first, long spine, then fold; consider the supported version, especially with osteoporosis (Bone Coach).

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Raises tension and, with high blood pressure, adds strain. Fix: slow breath through the nose and long exhale.

commonMistakes.title: Pressing the belly in a later pregnancy with knees together
commonMistakes.text: Pressing the belly in a later pregnancy with knees together. Compresses the abdomen. Fix: knees wide so the belly has room, or the bolster version (Prenatal Yoga Center and other prenatal sources).

commonMistakes.title: Rushing out of the pose
commonMistakes.text: Rushing out of the pose. Dizziness from a head-down fold, especially with low or high blood pressure. Fix: roll up slowly and pause kneeling for a breath.

commonMistakes.title: Treating it as a calorie burner
commonMistakes.text: Treating it as a calorie burner. It is a rest pose at about 2.3 MET (est.). Fix: use it to recover between harder poses.

safetyNotes: Knees: Several teaching sources say avoid the pose with a current or recent knee injury, or a knee arthritis flare, unless taught by an experienced teacher; if you continue, place a blanket or bolster between the seat and the heels, roll a towel behind the knees, widen the knees, or choose another pose (Lessons.com, Expanding Light, Bodybyyoga, DoYouYoga). Stop if knee pain persists.
Ankles and hips: pad under the ankles with a rolled towel; stop with sharp pain in the ankle, hip or groin. Hip, knee or ankle injuries are reasons to check with a clinician (Bodybyyoga).
Lower back: the knees-wide, supported version is gentle on the back in most teaching sources; do not force the fold, stop with increased back pain or leg symptoms.

Osteoporosis or bone thinning: Bone Coach teaches a modified Child's Pose with the spine neutral and the forehead supported so the neck and upper back do not round. A physician-led case series (Sinaki, Pain Practice, 2013, as cited in a search summary) linked yoga spinal-flexion positions to vertebral compression fractures in people with low bone density. With a diagnosed fracture or low bone density, ask a doctor or physio before holding the pose.

Pregnancy: the knees should be kept apart (wide) so the belly has room; avoid compressing the abdomen; use a bolster or pillows under the chest and belly in later pregnancy (Prenatal Yoga Center and other prenatal sources). Opinions differ: most prenatal teaching pages say the pose is fine through pregnancy with changes, one OB/GYN quoted in mindbodygreen says to avoid it in the third trimester (or second trimester with twins) over blood-flow concerns. This is not settled; check with your midwife or doctor. Tommy's advice is to avoid lying on the back for long periods after 16 weeks and to keep breathing steadily, which this pose (kneeling and folded forward) does not conflict with.

Blood pressure: Lessons.com advises avoiding prolonged holds with the head below the heart for high blood pressure or inner ear infections; other lists name very low blood pressure. The AYUSH CYP summary for Shashankasana lists high blood pressure, heart disease and hernia as cautions. Rise slowly and keep the head only slightly low, using a bolster.
Diarrhoea: a few teaching lists include it (Lessons.com, Sri Sri Yoga page), but a clinical reason was not found.
Neck: rest the forehead so the neck stays long; do not twist the neck under load.
Recent surgery (abdomen, knee, hip, spine): wait for the surgeon or physio before folding forward over the thighs.
Stop immediately if you feel: sharp or pinching pain in a knee, ankle or hip; tingling or numbness in a leg; dizziness, chest pain or breathlessness; pressure or pain in the belly (pregnancy).
Gym etiquette: use the stretching area or a mat out of walkways; wipe the mat after use.

Knees wide vs together: wide gives belly and chest room and is the pregnancy choice; together suits tight hips or a sensitive low back in some teaching. We chose wide as the default and offer together as a variation.
Arms forward vs back: forward gives more shoulder stretch; back (palms up) is the more relaxed Balasana version in some schools, while Shashankasana reaches forward. We offer both.
Hold time: 30 s to 3 min in teaching sources; yin holds longer; ACSM 10-30 s per stretch. We chose 30-60 s for beginners.
Pregnancy: most prenatal pages say fine with changes (wide knees, bolster); one quoted OB/GYN says avoid it in the third trimester. We chose "modify" with a check-with-midwife flag.
Osteoporosis: Bone Coach teaches a modified version; a case series links flexion yoga to fractures. We chose "modify" with props and a doctor check for a known fracture.

Blood pressure: some lists say avoid head-down holds with high blood pressure, others name low blood pressure; the CYP summary lists high blood pressure. We chose "modify" with a slight head-down and slow rise.
Evidence strength: no trial tests Child's Pose alone; benefits are described as teaching claims or from multi-pose programmes.
Official AYUSH step text: Not found (booklet could not be read); CYP details are from secondary summaries.
